feature: Marketing Free Scan page (/scan) — the consent screen renders its real hero copy and form controls, and the consent → scan transition fires with the entered domain flowing through to the live scanner header
notes: Marketing rebuild Part 2. Recreated from Design/design_handoff_marketing/Marketing Free Scan.dc.html
into artifacts/shane-mccaw-consulting/src/marketing/pages/FreeScan.tsx (route /scan, already wired
in App.tsx by the Part 0 scaffold).
SCOPE OF THIS MANIFEST — what is deterministically assertable:
1. GET /scan mounts the real page (data-testid=freescan-page), not the SPA 404 fallback.
2. The start phase renders its real, final hero copy ('...Microsoft 365 tenant.') and the three
consent-form controls (domain input, work-email input, the Connect-and-start button with its
real label). This is the site's primary conversion entry point.
3. Entering a domain + email, ticking the consent box, and clicking Connect transitions the page
into the scanning phase (data-testid=freescan-scanning) and the entered domain is echoed in the
live scanner header ('Scanning contoso.com') — proving the input flows through and the
consent-gated Start button is wired, without depending on the animation itself.
DELIBERATELY NOT ASSERTED, documented honestly rather than faked: the six-sector scanner animation
and the results screen. Per the handoff README's 'Out of scope' list the scan is SIMULATED on timers
(no Graph call), and the whole run is ~9.6s of stepped animation + a 900ms settle before results.
That timing is not a stable target for a static `expect` sample, and every number on the results
screen (findings, licence-waste figures, the monitoring quote) is authored demo data, not live
tenant data, so asserting it would only re-check a fixture. The reliably-real surface — the consent
screen and the transition into scanning — is what is covered here.
DEPLOYED-ORIGIN CAVEAT (same class the sibling marketing manifests carry): this asserts against
{{DEPLOY_URL}}, which only reflects the new marketing site — and this page — once that site is
redeployed. Until the Part 0+ rebuild is the deployed frontend, /scan resolves to the old site's
404 fallback and these steps fail on that ground alone, not on a page defect.
